clue.text: Stain the chest in the study

indicators.note: the chest is placed inside the study, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Someone notices a mark on a piece of furniture kept in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: To darken something is to discolour or blacken it, a synonym of stain.

clue.text: Fitness aid for boxers lacking a ring

explanation.surface: A piece of gym kit used by fighters who have no ring to train in.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbbell is a short weighted bar for exercise; split as words, a dumb bell is a silent one that gives no peal.

clue.text: Note golf score, competent but may be improved

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
par is the standard score for a hole in golf
able means competent or capable

explanation.surface: A golfer's round is noted as decent but with room for improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reparable can be mended, so it is capable of being put right.

clue.text: Sheep's quarters

parts.note: the compass quarters are the points east, west and south, abbreviated to single letters
W is the abbreviation for west, a compass quarter
E is the abbreviation for east, a compass quarter
S is the abbreviation for south, a compass quarter

explanation.surface: A question about where a flock is housed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; 'quarters' looks like lodgings but means the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, so the plural noun is a kind of sheep.

clue.text: Joined in, without being searched

indicators.note: here 'without' has its old sense of outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enrolled in a club without having to be frisked first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined is a synonym of joined: brought together into one.

clue.text: Dump a sub-standard cargo

explanation.surface: An order to get rid of a shipment of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload is to unload or get rid of; split as words, an off load is a cargo that has gone bad.

clue.text: Edna's kebab is mixed with cheap tinned food

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up like the ingredients of a dish

parts.note: taken as written, with the s of the possessive kept

explanation.surface: Edna's takeaway kebab is served together with a can of something cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot beans stewed in tomato sauce and sold in tins are a staple budget food.

clue.text: S. African's place of birth?

explanation.surface: A question about where a South African was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal; natal is also an adjective meaning relating to birth.

clue.text: Put new pep into endless diet with port

indicators.note: one set of letters is put into the other
endless means the final letter of the word is cut off
new means the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A dietitian revamps a tired diet by adding a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts DIET to DIE; 'new' rearranges PEP to EPP, which goes 'into' DIE. 'Port' looks like wine but is the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French harbour town on the English Channel coast.

clue.text: Keen to have jellied eel in the the salad?

indicators.note: the first word is made to have the other inside it

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to cry

indicators.note: jellied suggests the letters are set in a new form like a mould

explanation.surface: A diner keen on jellied eels wonders whether they belong in a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager but is the verb meaning to wail in mourning. 'Jellied' rearranges the eel into ELE. The doubled 'the' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a crisp stalk vegetable commonly eaten raw as a salad ingredient.

clue.text: Wooden part of a table, a symbol of Canada

explanation.surface: A description of a piece of furniture made of a Canadian timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is a hinged or removable part of a table top, here made of maple wood; the red leaf of the maple tree is Canada's national emblem.

clue.text: Girl I take out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters have been put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are taking a young woman out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Katie is a common female forename, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: In Italy a singer lacks tone

indicators.note: the singer lacks something, so those letters are taken away from him

parts.note: a baritone is a male singer with a voice between tenor and bass
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian vocalist is criticised for poor tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a location: the answer is a place found in Italy, a port on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is an Adriatic port city in southern Italy, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: The cricketer makes another mistake

explanation.surface: A sports report on a fielder who keeps erring.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a fielding position beside the wicketkeeper is named second slip, after the man standing there; a second error would equally be another slip.

clue.text: A bouncer at the gym club

definitions.text: A bouncer at the gym club

parts.words: A bouncer at the gym club
parts.note: a bouncer suggests a doorman, but here it is equipment that people bounce on in a gymnasium

explanation.surface: A doorman working at a fitness club.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung canvas sheet on a frame that gymnasts jump on.

clue.text: Precious possession one is not bound to have

definitions.text: Precious possession one is not bound to have

parts.words: Precious possession one is not bound to have
parts.note: reads like something one need not own, but 'not bound' means free of chains, a prized state

explanation.surface: A remark about a treasured belonging that nobody is obliged to keep.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom is the state of not being tied or imprisoned, which is a valued thing to possess.

clue.text: Is afraid of disturbing adders

indicators.note: disturbing the snakes stirs up and rearranges the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fears upsetting a nest of venomous snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it, so a person who dreads is afraid.

clue.text: Import teak, say, brought in by sea

parts.note: drift means gist or import, as in catching someone's drift
teak is an example of a wood

explanation.surface: A timber merchant imports teak, which arrives by ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' looks like a verb about trade but is the noun meaning sense or gist.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood is timber washed ashore by the waves, carried to land by the water.

clue.text: Stock market reaction to panic?

parts.note: reads as a financial crash, but stock here means cattle, rushing off in fright

explanation.surface: A question about how financial markets respond to fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden frightened rush of a herd of cattle or horses.

clue.text: A money changer who had a farm

indicators.note: the letters given are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bureau de change clerk who once owned some farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money changer' looks like one job; 'changer' is the anagram signal applied to A MONEY. The definition reads as 'one who had a farm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a yeoman was a small landowner who farmed his own land.

clue.text: Writer is uplifted by air or sea

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up a word reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: An author is cheered by fresh air or a trip to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is uplifted' turns PEN to NEP in this down clue. 'Air' looks like the atmosphere but is a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, the Roman god of the sea, is used poetically to stand for the ocean itself.

clue.text: After multiple gigs new trio perform-term without restraint

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'After multiple gigs new trio perform-term without restraint'; RUN (multiple gigs) + RIOT (anagram of trio) fit, but 'perform-term' is garbled OCR and no source gives the printed text, so the definition cannot be fixed.
annotationWithheld.clue: After multiple gigs new trio perform-term without restraint

clue.text: Fame made owner change name

indicators.note: the owner is told to change, so the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Becoming famous led a proprietor to adopt a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' gives RENOW; the abbreviation for name then follows it, outside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is widespread acclaim, a synonym of fame.

clue.text: Get on a bit maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints the words could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: An encouragement to hurry up a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or get it.

clue.text: Friendly Society? No, and unlikely to be profitable

explanation.surface: A comment that an unfriendly mutual society is unlikely to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad company means unsuitable companions, the opposite of friendly society; read literally it is also a business firm doing poorly.

clue.text: Defeatism lacking achievement leads to a belief in God

indicators.note: the first word is lacking the second, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement

explanation.surface: Giving up hope without having accomplished anything leads someone to faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene in the world, a form of faith in a deity.

clue.text: Stop! This is a hold up!

explanation.surface: A robber shouts at a victim during a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop it; the stem of a plant holds up its flower or leaves.

clue.text: A slight incoherence in speech

explanation.surface: A small lack of clarity in the way someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insult or slight on someone's character; slurring is running words together indistinctly.

clue.text: One wasn't there to provide such a defence

definitions.text: One wasn't there to provide such a defence

parts.words: One wasn't there to provide such a defence
parts.note: the plea of having been elsewhere when a crime happened is what a suspect offers in court

explanation.surface: A suspect pleads that he was absent at the time of the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being somewhere else when an offence took place, used as a legal defence.

clue.text: Clue women possibly find displeasing

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A solver remarks that some women dislike a certain crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted, so it is displeasing to receive.

clue.text: Told off

parts.note: reads as scolded, but 'told' can mean counted, so counted off one by one

explanation.definitionFit: To number people is to count them, as soldiers in a line call out their positions; 'told' is an old word for counted.

clue.text: A game one may come across

explanation.surface: An invitation to play a card game with a passing visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players; a bridge is also a structure for crossing a river or road.
